segments.text: One egg peels smooth, the other tears apart.
You'd think the fresher egg peels easier.
But it's the opposite - fresher eggs peel worse.
Eggshells are covered in tiny invisible pores.
Over time, carbon dioxide seeps out through them.
As it escapes, the egg white turns more alkaline.
That loosens its grip on the inner membrane.
So the older the egg, the easier the shell comes off.
